Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Prenatal genetic testing at 16 weeks gestation. Advanced maternal age (39 years).
Clinical Indication: Screening for Down syndrome and other chromosomal abnormalities

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded Chromosome Analysis (Karyotype)

METHODOLOGY
Amniotic fluid cells were cultured according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were harvested and G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa staining. A minimum of 20 metaphase cells were analyzed at the 400-550 band level of resolution. Two independent cultures were established to minimize the risk of maternal cell contamination and culture artifacts.

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XY

Normal male karyotype

No evidence of trisomy 21 or other chromosomal abnormalities detected at this level of resolution.

Number of cells analyzed: 20
Number of cells counted: 5
Number of cultures analyzed: 2

INTERPRETATION
This analysis reveals a normal male karyotype with no evidence of numerical or structural chromosomal abnormalities. Specifically, there is no evidence of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), or sex chromosome abnormalities.

These results supersede any previous rapid PCR analysis performed on this specimen.

LIMITATIONS
This test can detect numerical abnormalities and structural rearrangements larger than 5-10 Mb. Smaller deletions, duplications, or balanced rearrangements may not be detected. This test does not rule out single gene disorders, uniparental disomy, or low-level mosaicism (<10%).

RECOMMENDATIONS
The results indicate a chromosomally normal male fetus. No additional cytogenetic testing is indicated based on these findings. Results should be discussed with the referring physician and/or genetic counselor in the context of other clinical findings and screening results.
